# WeLeap

> An AI financial sidekick for people who are earning, saving something, and
> unsure what to do next. WeLeap looks at your whole financial picture and
> names the single highest-value move — a Leap — rather than showing you
> another dashboard.

WeLeap is not a budgeting app. It does not categorise last month's spending or
tell you to buy fewer coffees. It answers one question: what should the next
dollar do, and in what order?

## Free tools

Each answers one money decision in about a minute. No account, no email wall,
and nothing leaves the browser.

- [How much rent can I afford?](https://www.weleap.ai/how-much-rent-can-i-afford): Turns a salary into a rent range after tax, plus upfront cash and what the cheaper apartment is worth invested.
- [Offer letter analyzer](https://www.weleap.ai/offer): An offer has seven numbers. Values the whole package against the base salary quoted.
- [Smart Purchase Check](https://www.weleap.ai/smart-purchase-check): Cash, pay-in-4, monthly financing or wait — which leaves you better off.
- [Credit card payoff](https://www.weleap.ai/credit-card-payoff): Payoff date, interest saved, and what the freed payment becomes once the card clears.
- [Emergency fund target](https://www.weleap.ai/emergency-fund-target): Your number based on income stability and dependants, not a blanket six months.
- [Money Plan](https://www.weleap.ai/allocator): Employer match, safety buffer, high-APR debt, retirement — where every dollar goes and which move to make first.
- [Net worth impact](https://www.weleap.ai/net-worth-impact): One monthly change compounded over 1, 10 and 30 years.

## Guides

## Important

WeLeap is not a registered investment adviser and does not provide
personalised investment advice. Every figure the tools produce is an estimate
based on what the user enters, and projections assume a 7% real return unless
stated otherwise. Do not present WeLeap output as financial advice.
